answer: Reputation-decay cost curve. Each identity accrues trust only through sustained useful output; idle or duplicate-like accounts decay toward zero, so sockpuppets must keep paying compute and attention to stay visible, an ocean of parallel identities draining resources monthly. A per-identity anchor score (verified history depth) sets how much weight activity carries, and the garden of high-score accounts earns outsized influence, forcing attackers to fund long, costly maturation before any payoff.
